# Supatype

> Zero drift: one set of TypeScript types runs the whole stack, database to component. Define `Model<>` types and Supatype derives the Postgres tables, migrations, row-level security, REST and GraphQL APIs, auth, storage, realtime, Studio editing views and the typed client your components use. Change a field once; rename a field and the build fails instead of production.

Supatype is a type-first backend platform on real Postgres 17. The TypeScript schema is the single source of truth; SQL, policies, APIs, the typed client and admin UI are generated from it rather than kept in step by hand. `supatype dev` runs the full stack locally (Docker Compose by default), applies schema changes as you save and regenerates the typed client. Production can self-host with Docker Compose (`supatype self-host compose up`) or use Supatype Cloud (EU-hosted, coming soon: join the waiting list at https://www.supatype.com/#cloud).

Licensing: client SDKs, framework bindings and plugins are MIT; the CLI, Studio and services are Apache 2.0; the schema engine is source-available under the Business Source License 1.1 (production use allowed except offering a competing hosted service or product; each version becomes Apache 2.0 four years after release).

Primary audience: TypeScript developers on Postgres who want end-to-end type safety without stitching a backend, a separate CMS and hand-written migrations together.

Official site: https://www.supatype.com/
Organization: https://github.com/supatype
Contact: GitHub and Discord, linked from the site. Licensing questions: licensing@supatype.com

## Docs & guides

- [Docs](https://www.supatype.com/docs/): Local development, self-hosting, deploying changes, upgrading, plus the guides below
- [Schema](https://www.supatype.com/docs/schema.html): Models, field types, relations, access rules, field rules and masking, drafts and versions, slugs, rich text, blocks, buckets, auth user ids, renames, what a push refuses
- [Client](https://www.supatype.com/docs/client.html): `@supatype/client` from the generated file: queries, filters, embeds, writes, drafts and publishing, auth, storage, realtime, functions, errors
- [Frameworks](https://www.supatype.com/docs/frameworks.html): React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and React Native bindings, and @supatype/ssr server clients for Next.js
- [Auth](https://www.supatype.com/docs/auth.html): Email and password, magic links, phone codes and OAuth, sessions and tokens, how tokens reach access rules, the React and React Native auth UI
- [Storage](https://www.supatype.com/docs/storage.html): Buckets declared in the schema, file and image fields, bucket access rules, uploads, signed URLs, image transforms, limits
- [Realtime](https://www.supatype.com/docs/realtime.html): Table changes filtered by read access and field rules, filters, broadcast and presence, React and Vue hooks
- [Functions](https://www.supatype.com/docs/functions.html): TypeScript functions on Deno at /functions/v1, the caller's token, secrets, local dev and self-host
- [Seeding](https://www.supatype.com/docs/seeding.html): `seeds/*.ts`, the generated builder, create vs upsert, nested children, relations by key, `expr.default()`, sign-in users, `supatype seed`
- [Studio](https://www.supatype.com/docs/studio.html): The CMS and admin app generated from your models: editors, rich text, media, drafts and versions, live preview, API docs, GraphQL explorer, SQL runner, history
- [Studio roles](https://www.supatype.com/docs/studio-roles.html): Admin, developer, editor and viewer: what each can do, full access vs Studio mode, masking, Send as, drafts and publishing, granting roles
- [CLI reference](https://www.supatype.com/docs/cli.html): Every supatype command with its subcommands and main flags
- [Local development](https://www.supatype.com/docs/#local-dev): `supatype init` and `supatype dev` run a full local stack
- [Self-hosting](https://www.supatype.com/docs/#self-host): Docker Compose on a server you own
- [Upgrading](https://www.supatype.com/docs/#upgrading): Updating images and binaries, then pushing the schema
- [Running in production](https://www.supatype.com/docs/#production): Status, logs, backups with pg_dump, and rolling back a push
- [Upgrade notes for 0.7.0](https://github.com/supatype/supatype/blob/main/UPGRADING.md): Ownership checks, declared renames, identity columns, realtime DELETE rules, lock waits, licence
- [VM deploy with GitHub Actions](https://www.supatype.com/deploy-vm-github-actions.html): Self-host deploy path using GitHub Actions onto a VM
- [Coming from Supabase](https://www.supatype.com/from-supabase.html): How Supabase tables, RLS, supabase-js, storage, auth, realtime and functions map to Supatype, and adopting existing tables
- [Coming from Prisma](https://www.supatype.com/from-prisma.html): How schema.prisma, prisma migrate and Prisma Client map to Supatype types, push and the typed client
- [Changelog](https://www.supatype.com/changelog.html): What changed in each release
- [Agent skill](https://github.com/supatype/supatype/tree/main/skills/supatype): Schema, config, CLI and self-host reference for coding agents

## Platform capabilities

- [Migrations](https://www.supatype.com/#how-it-works): The Rust schema engine diffs types against the live database, classifies each change as safe, cautious or destructive, applies it in one transaction with a recorded rollback, and never guesses a rename (renames are declared with `supatype rename`)
- [Access rules](https://www.supatype.com/#how-it-works): `Public`, `LoggedIn`, `Owner<>`, `OwnerFrom<>`, `Role<>` on models and fields compile to Postgres row-level security
- [Studio](https://www.supatype.com/#how-it-works): Schema-generated admin and CMS: lists, forms, rich text, blocks, media library, drafts, versions, live preview. Four roles on self-host (admin, developer, editor, viewer; Cloud adds owner and billing); the SQL editor is for admins and developers, and owners on Cloud
- [Storage](https://www.supatype.com/#how-it-works): `Bucket<>` types with accept lists, size limits and access rules; image transforms; time-limited signed URLs
- [Realtime](https://www.supatype.com/#how-it-works): Change subscriptions, presence and broadcast; each event, deletes included, reaches only subscribers allowed to read that row
- [APIs](https://www.supatype.com/#how-it-works): REST through PostgREST and GraphQL through pg_graphql, both running as the caller so row-level security applies. PostgREST 14; in production, browsers may call the API from the site URL and the origins you allow
